question: Refer to the exhibit. A network engineer plans to upgrade the current software images of a Cisco Nexus switch. What is the impact of starting the EPLD upgrade?
context:
switch# show install all impact epld n9000-epld.9.2.1.img
Compatibility check:
Module  Type   Upgradable  Impact      Reason
------  -----  ----------  ----------  --------
  1     SUP    YES         disruptive  Module Upgradable

Retrieving EPLD versions... Please wait.

Images will be upgraded according to following table:
Module  Type  EPLD       Running-Version  New-Version  Upg-Required
------  ----  ---------  ---------------  -----------  ------------
  1     SUP   MI FPGA    0x23             0x23         No
  1     SUP   IO FPGA    0x06             0x06         No
  1     SUP   MI FPGA2   0x23             0x23         No
options: The switch reboots one time for the new EPLD versions to take effect.
The switch reboots multiple times for the new EPLD versions to take effect.
The switch skips the EPLD upgrade for each EPLD device of the switch.
The switch skips the EPLD upgrade for MIFPGA and proceeds with the other EPLD devices.
theory: EPLD upgrades only touch the specific programmable hardware components (FPGAs/CPLDs) whose running version differs from the new image's version; the switch skips any EPLD device whose Running-Version already matches the New-Version. In the exhibited output, every listed EPLD (MI FPGA, IO FPGA, MI FPGA2) already shows "Upg-Required: No" because running and new versions are identical, so the switch will skip the EPLD upgrade for every device on that module rather than reboot or selectively upgrade one type. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — EPLD Upgrades)
